acceptance_signals: The exact Markdown candidate lists each eligible record using only its date, title, and stable relative link, with no inline source SHA-256 value.
The strict agentgov.documentation-archive-plan 1.0 JSON entries retain every source SHA-256 value, and the candidate change retains before and after content digests.
Stable newest-date and same-day path ordering, explicit through-date behavior, title warnings, create, update, no-op, failure, advisory, and not-applicable states remain unchanged.
Fixture tests prove compact Markdown rendering, retained machine-readable integrity evidence, existing-index update and no-op behavior, and filesystem no-mutation behavior.
README and the dedicated guide explain the human-readable versus machine-verifiable evidence split without claiming that usefulness is deterministic.
A real-repository read-only run through 2026-08-15 produces 16 linked entries without inline source hashes and does not create docs/development-log/INDEX.md.
Focused archive, user-documentation, and task-contract tests, the complete unittest suite, task and repository governance checks, and git diff --check pass.

decision.rationale: On 2026-08-15 Compact Documentation Index Candidate v1 delivered the admitted compact Markdown presentation while retaining machine-readable source hashes, candidate-content digests, deterministic states, and all read-only authority boundaries. The focused archive, user-documentation, and task-contract tests passed; the complete suite passed all 821 tests with 2 platform-limited skips; the real-repository no-mutation run, task and repository checks, admitted-state scope inspection, and git diff --check completed with only the pre-existing excluded local configuration outside task scope. A distinct native current-Agent self-review found no correction-required requirement, architecture, scope, implementation, or data drift. This paused task authorizes no index write, writer, schedule, reminder, Git action, publication, release, deployment, or follow-on implementation.

requirement.summary: Refine the read-only documentation archive planner so its exact human-facing INDEX.md candidate renders compact date, title, and relative-link bullets without inline source hashes, while preserving per-record SHA-256 values in the strict JSON entries and preserving all existing deterministic ordering, change digests, no-mutation behavior, advisory usefulness semantics, and denied writer, scheduling, Git, publication, release, and deployment authority.

items: Removing hashes from both human and machine surfaces would weaken existing integrity evidence.
Changing candidate bytes alters create, update, no-op, and after-digest expectations and requires focused regression coverage.
Documentation could overstate usefulness as objective rather than advisory.
A planner change could accidentally create the index or mutate dated logs if no-mutation protection regresses.
Unrelated user-owned workspace changes could be misattributed unless scope remains explicit.
Reviewed assumption: Removing inline source hashes from candidate Markdown improves scanability while JSON entries remain the machine-verifiable integrity surface.
Reviewed assumption: The strict schema shape and version remain unchanged because all existing fields and semantics are preserved; only the rendered Markdown presentation becomes compact.
Reviewed assumption: Terminal diagnostic ENTRY lines may retain hashes because this task targets the proposed human-facing INDEX.md artifact, not diagnostic output.
Reviewed assumption: The existing read-only command and ten-minute adoption journey remain unchanged.
Reviewed assumption: The pre-existing untracked .codex configuration is human-owned and excluded.
Reviewed unknown: Whether product owners find the compact candidate sufficiently useful remains a later human review outcome.
Reviewed unknown: Any repository writer, concurrency contract, scheduling, reminder, or publication workflow remains undecided and separately gated.

title: Refine compact documentation index candidate v1
